findings.claim: The change rewrites the app-wide SidebarProvider, ThemeProvider and ProfileProvider so they no longer render bare children before hydration, and none of the three is in the touch-point list.
findings.impact: These providers wrap every page, not only player files. The diff removes the post-hydration remount of the whole app subtree. Any component that relied on that remount now keeps its first-render state. The r5fix review records one such effect: an attribute-only hydration mismatch now stays stale. So the change reaches every route, outside the declared scope of SPEC-CORE-085..090.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/SidebarProvider.tsx:100-117 drops `if (!hydrated) return <>{children}</>` and exposes `hydrated && isOpen` and `hydrated && isOverlay`. ThemeProvider.tsx drops the `mounted` state and its bare-children branch. ProfileProvider.tsx replaces `mounted` with a `wroteNickname` ref so a child's mount-effect write is not overwritten. A new test, frontend/src/components/__tests__/SidebarProviderHydration.test.tsx, covers this. None of these paths appears in Touch points, and r1/classification.json lists all four among zones_touched.

bucket_proposal.reason: No declared invariant covers app-wide provider hydration. The paths are not in the touch-point list, and the change reaches every page.

findings.proposed_fix: Add the three providers and their hydration test to the touch points, with the reason (the remount broke I4 single-mount on first load), or split them into their own change.

findings.claim: The shared `SlotEntryRenderer` in AddonSlot.tsx gains an `onRendered` prop and a `RenderedSignal` child, and AddonSlot.tsx is not in the touch-point list.
findings.impact: `SlotEntryRenderer` renders entries for every slot that uses it, not only `player-side`. The new signal decides whether a pending `player-side` entry counts as available (revised I1). An entry whose module fails to load never signals, so it never gets a toggle. That rule now lives in a shared component that the declared scope does not name.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/AddonSlot.tsx:59-118 adds `onRendered` and `RenderedSignal` inside `<Suspense>`. useSlotAvailability.ts adds `isPending`/`renderedFor`; that file is listed, but AddonSlot.tsx is not.

bucket_proposal.reason: This implements revised I1 correctly as far as I read it, but it is a shared component that the touch-point list omits.

findings.proposed_fix: List frontend/src/components/AddonSlot.tsx (SlotEntryRenderer `onRendered`) in the touch points.

findings.claim: docs/addons/media-import.md is changed, and it is not among the nine documents the touch points and §9 list.
findings.impact: No user-facing defect. The doc now says the `.loft` panel is in the Info tab under the title, which follows the D-14 revision of I7. The touch-point list did not anticipate this doc.
findings.evidence: The diff changes the media-import.md heading from 'Below the player' to 'Where the details are'. r1/classification.json lists docs/addons/media-import.md. The Touch points 'Docs, all as §9 lists' omits it.

bucket_proposal.reason: This is an unplanned path, and the content is consistent with the revised I7.

findings.proposed_fix: Add docs/addons/media-import.md to the touch-point docs list.

findings.claim: The `loft-metadata` slot moves from under the player into the Info tab on the canonical page, through a new `loftMetadata` prop on FileMetaBlock, a new `showMetadataAside` prop on MediaPlayerBlock, a new `-mx-4 md:mx-0` inset on the collection aside, and a new globals.css grid rule. The touch points' descriptions of those files do not mention any of this.
findings.impact: A `.loft` file's channel, date and description move to a different place on every surface. The commit under review, 7f2b9ae52, changes this aside's inset on the collection surface. The work is covered by the D-14 revision of I7, but the touch-point descriptions of FileDetailContainer, MediaPlayerBlock and FileMetaBlock list other items: description, layoutToggle, preview-actions and the clamp.
findings.evidence: FileDetailContainer.tsx builds `loftMetadata` (ridesShell && loft && hasSlot). FileMetaBlock.tsx renders it under `data-inspector-header-loft-metadata`. MediaPlayerBlock.tsx adds `showMetadataAside` and, when framed, the `-mx-4 md:mx-0` aside class. globals.css adds a `[data-inspector-header-loft-metadata]` grid-area rule. The new LoftMetadataPlacement.test.tsx and collection-workbench-metrics-desktop.spec.ts (the 390px inset) test it. The ADDON-DEVELOPMENT.md changelog adds a third row, while §9 says two.

bucket_proposal.reason: This is a behaviour the revised I7 covers, but the touch-point entries of the files it changes do not mention it.

findings.proposed_fix: Extend the touch points: the `loft-metadata` placement in FileDetailContainer, FileMetaBlock, MediaPlayerBlock and globals.css, plus LoftMetadataPlacement.test.tsx.

findings.claim: Several test and test-registration files are added or changed outside the touch-point list: e2e-components/projects.ts, spec-viewport.spec.ts, componentFixtureParity.test.tsx, src/__tests__/mediaLayoutRemoved.test.ts, and the new FileDetail tests Workbench, WorkbenchCollection, WorkbenchPendingEntry, LoftMetadataPlacement and workbenchHelpers.ts.
findings.impact: None for users. These are scaffolding for the planned new real-browser and unit cases, and the list simply does not name them. FileDetailContent.test.tsx, which the list names under scaffolding, is also changed.
findings.evidence: r1/classification.json zones_touched includes all of these paths. The Touch points name only the generic 'new real-browser cases' and the harness/setup files.

bucket_proposal.reason: These are unplanned test paths and break no invariant.

findings.proposed_fix: List the new test files and the e2e project registrations in the touch points.

specification_compliance: The touch-point files that were changed match their stated purpose: ShellLayout, MediaCanvas, MediaPlayerBlock, FileDetailCanvas, FileDetailPresenter, FileDetailContainer, FileMetaBlock, FileDescription, tabs.ts, InspectorShell, useSlotAvailability, useCompanionMetrics, mediaHostStyle, layoutSizes, the workbench files, workbenchPanels store, the MediaLayoutToggle and mediaLayout removals, preferenceInitScript, globals.css, ActiveSummaryHost, messages, the intelligence addon and the listed docs.

Some listed touch points show no change in this diff: app/layout.tsx, ChaptersPanel.tsx, FileDetailShell.tsx, FileDetailFullScreen.tsx, e2e scenes-section*.spec.ts and fixtures/scenesSection.tsx, and several of the scaffolding tests (FileDetailPageRow, FileNavInPageRow, FileDetailInboxNav, PlainTextDocument, FindInFile.epub, TreeYield*). That is the opposite direction to the question asked and is not reported as a finding.

The question asked: the diff reaches these paths outside the touch-point list: SidebarProvider/ThemeProvider/ProfileProvider and their hydration test, AddonSlot.tsx, docs/addons/media-import.md, the loft-metadata relocation inside listed files, and test registration and new test files.
potential_unspecified_behavior: App-wide provider hydration no longer remounts the page subtree (Sidebar, Theme and Profile providers). Neither the spec nor its invariants describe this.

SlotEntryRenderer's onRendered signal is a new pending state for addon entries. Revised I1 states the rule for player-side, but the shared component now carries it for any caller that passes onRendered.
regression_risks: Provider changes affect every route. A component that reads client-only state in a render-time initializer and shows it only through an attribute now keeps the server value (r5fix F1).
ThemeProvider and ProfileProvider consumers now see the pre-read values ('system', a null nickname) inside a real context before the stored value is read, where before they saw the default context.
test_coverage: SidebarProviderHydration.test.tsx covers the single mount for all three providers and the overlay request made from a child's mount effect.
WorkbenchPendingEntry.test.tsx covers the AddonSlot onRendered path, including a lazy chunk.
LoftMetadataPlacement.test.tsx and collection-workbench-metrics-desktop.spec.ts cover the loft-metadata placement and the 390px inset.
not_verified: I could not run git, so I could not isolate the files touched by commit 7f2b9ae52 alone from the whole-branch diff provided. My findings are against the diff as given.
I ran no tests (unit or e2e).
I did not check whether the listed but unchanged e2e scenes-section specs still pass now that scenes has moved to player-side.
